activity.title: Activity
activity.subtitle: Operations run against Docker

activity.emptyBody: Every action the app performs on Docker will appear here with its equivalent command, status and result.
activity.equivalentNote: Approximate translation. The operation was performed through the Docker Engine API, not by running this command.
activity.noEquivalent: This operation has no exact docker command equivalent.
activity.truncated: Output truncated: showing the first {{shown}} of {{total}} bytes.
activity.loadError: Could not load the activity history: {{message}}

settings.openOnError: Open the panel when an operation fails

conn.notConnectedTitle: This section needs a Docker connection
conn.notConnectedBody: There is no connection to Docker Engine. The Dashboard explains the cause and how to fix it.
conn.autoRetry: The app retries automatically every few seconds.

diag.title: Connection diagnosis
diag.candidatesHint: In the order they are searched.
diag.rootGroupWarning: Being in the {{group}} group is equivalent to having administrator privileges on this computer. The safer alternative is rootless Docker.
diag.noAutoFix: Docker Control Center does not change system permissions or groups: you need to run these steps yourself in a terminal.

noSocket.title: Docker Engine not found
noSocket.body: There is no Docker socket in the usual locations.

notInstalled.title: Docker does not seem to be installed
notInstalled.body: No socket, Docker CLI or Docker daemon was found.

daemonNotRunning.title: Docker Engine is stopped
daemonNotRunning.body: The socket {{path}} exists, but no process is answering on it.

permissionDenied.title: No permission to use the Docker socket
permissionDenied.body: Your user ({{user}}) cannot open {{path}}. It belongs to {{owner}}:{{group}} with mode {{mode}}.

unsupportedHost.title: Unsupported Docker connection
unsupportedHost.body: DOCKER_HOST or the active context point to {{host}}. This version only supports local Unix sockets.

invalidPath.title: The configured path is not valid

notASocket.title: The path is not a socket
notASocket.body: {{path}} exists, but it is not a Unix socket.

notDocker.title: The socket does not respond like Docker
notDocker.body: {{path}} accepts connections but does not respond like the Docker Engine API: {{message}}

timeout.title: Docker is not responding in time
timeout.body: {{path}} did not respond within 5 seconds. The daemon may be stuck or overloaded.

apiTooOld.title: Docker version too old
apiTooOld.body: Docker Engine offers API {{api}} and {{min}} or later is required (Docker 20.10 or later).

stepsText.install: Install Docker Engine. With the Debian or Ubuntu packages:
stepsText.installOfficial: Or follow the official installation guide for Debian/Ubuntu at docs.docker.com/engine/install.
stepsText.startSystem: Start the Docker service and enable it at boot:
stepsText.startRootless: If you use rootless Docker, start your user service:
stepsText.checkStatus: If it does not start, check its status and latest messages:
stepsText.addGroup: Add your user to the {{group}} group:
stepsText.relogin: Then log out and log back in for the group to take effect.
stepsText.alreadyInGroup: You already belong to the {{group}} group, but your current session does not have it active yet. Log out and back in, or restart the computer.
stepsText.ownerUnexpected: The socket does not belong to the docker group. Check the SocketGroup option of the docker.socket unit.
stepsText.unsetHost: To use the local socket, remove DOCKER_HOST from your environment or switch back to the default context:
stepsText.customPath: Or set a specific Unix socket in Settings, Docker connection section.
stepsText.fixPath: Fix the path in Settings, Docker connection section. It must be absolute, for example /var/run/docker.sock.
stepsText.checkPath: Check that the path is Docker's socket and not another service.
stepsText.upgrade: Upgrade Docker Engine to 20.10 or later.
stepsText.retry: Once fixed, press “Reconnect”. The app also retries on its own.

settingsDocker.title: Docker connection
settingsDocker.autoHint: Looks for DOCKER_HOST, the active Docker context, your user's rootless socket and the system socket, in that order.
settingsDocker.customHint: Absolute path of a Unix socket, for example /run/user/1000/docker.sock.
settingsDocker.composeHint: Obtained by running “docker compose version”. Needed for the Docker Compose section (phase 7); the rest of the app works without it.
settingsDocker.security: Access to the Docker socket is equivalent to administrator privileges. The app never changes system permissions or groups.
settingsDocker.composeUnusable: The plugin is at {{path}} but the Docker CLI does not use it
settingsDocker.composeInstall: Install Docker Compose v2 (Debian 12 only ships v1, which is not supported: use Docker's official repository):

crash.body: Docker has not been affected. You can reload the window; if it happens again, copy this text to report it.

detail.duplicateFailed: Could not read the configuration to duplicate it: {{message}}
detail.notFound: Container {{name}} no longer exists in Docker.
detail.noPorts: No ports published on this computer.
detail.inspectHint: Full output of docker inspect {{name}}, exactly as Docker returns it.

logs.dropped: Only the last {{max}} lines are shown; older ones were discarded.

terminal.hint: Runs a shell with docker exec -it. Closing the session ends the shell.
terminal.notRunning: The container is not running: start it to open a terminal.

stats.notRunning: The container is not running: there are no statistics to show.
stats.formulaHint: Values computed like docker stats: CPU is a percentage of one CPU and memory excludes the page cache.

stream.failed: The stream ended with an error: {{message}}

create.title: Create container
create.notesTitle: Some settings of the original are not carried over:

f.name: Name
f.publishAll: Publish all exposed ports on free ports

h.name: Optional: if empty, Docker generates one.
h.image: Must exist on this computer (pulling arrives in phase 4).
h.argv: Split into arguments with shell-style quoting, but no shell is run.
h.entrypointMulti: Docker accepts a single executable in --entrypoint: the remaining items are sent at the start of the command.
h.volumeName: Empty = anonymous volume. Docker creates it if it doesn't exist.
h.user: Name or UID[:GID]. Empty = image default.

g.processHint: What runs when the container starts.
g.envHint: Values of keys such as PASSWORD or TOKEN are hidden on screen, but they are sent to Docker as-is and anyone with Docker access can read them.
g.portsHint: Publish container ports on this computer.
g.mountsHint: Docker volumes or folders on this computer (bind mounts).
g.restartHint: What Docker does when the main process exits.
g.capsHint: Comma separated, e.g. NET_ADMIN or ALL.

create.imageVolumes: The image declares volumes at {{paths}}. If you mount nothing there, Docker creates anonymous volumes.
create.imageNotLocal: Image {{ref}} is not on this computer. Docker won't pull it when creating the container; pull it first (phase 4) or choose a local one.
create.imageDefaultsError: Could not read the image configuration: {{message}}
create.equivalentHint: Equivalent Docker CLI command. The app doesn't run it: it sends the request to the API and records it in the activity panel.
create.bodyHint: Body of POST /containers/create that will be sent to Docker.
create.startFailed: The container was created but could not be started: {{message}}
create.secretsHidden_one: {{count}} sensitive value is shown as ******** here and in the activity panel; Docker receives it in full.
create.secretsHidden_other: {{count}} sensitive values are shown as ******** here and in the activity panel; Docker receives them in full.

name.invalid: Invalid name: use letters, digits, “_”, “.” or “-”, starting with a letter or digit.

argv.trailingEscape: Ends with a backslash with nothing after it.

path.notAbsolute: Must be an absolute path (start with /).

env.duplicate: {{key}} is repeated; the last value wins.

ports.ignoredWithNetwork: With the “{{network}}” network Docker ignores published ports.

port.privileged: Port {{port}} is privileged: it may fail with rootless Docker.

mount.targetInvalid: The container path must be absolute and not /.
mount.targetDuplicate: There is already a mount at {{target}}.

bind.missing: Folder {{path}} does not exist on this computer.
bind.sensitive: Mounting {{path}} writable gives the container control over the system. Mark it read-only if you don't need writes.

cpus.range: Enter a number of CPUs between 0.01 and 1024.

memory.reservationAboveLimit: The reservation cannot exceed the limit.

autoRemove.restart: “Remove when it exits” is not compatible with a restart policy.

issues.privileged: Privileged mode gives the container almost full access to the computer.

ref.invalidRepository: Invalid name: lowercase letters, digits and the separators . _ - only
ref.invalidTag: Invalid tag: letters, digits, _ . - (128 max, not starting with . or -).

context.huge: Using {{path}} as context would send a huge number of files.

dockerfile.invalid: Invalid path: it must be relative and inside the context.
dockerfile.missing: {{path}} does not exist in the context folder.

tags.none: Without a name, the image will show as <none>.

arg.secret: {{key}} looks like a secret: arguments stay in the image history.

driver.singleton: There can only be one network with the {{value}} driver (the predefined one).
driver.swarm: Overlay networks require Docker Swarm: without it, Docker will reject the creation.
driver.noParent: Without the "parent" option, the network has no way out through any physical interface.

subnet.required: Set the subnet to use a gateway or range.
subnet.hostBits: {{value}} is not a network address; it should be {{fixed}}.
subnet.family: {{value}} is not of this address family.

gateway.family: {{value}} is not of this address family.

ipRange.hostBits: {{value}} is not a network address; it should be {{fixed}}.
ipRange.family: {{value}} is not of this address family.

ipv6.disabled: Enable IPv6 to use an IPv6 subnet.

volumeName.short: The name must have at least two characters.
volumeName.invalid: Invalid name: use letters, digits, "_", "." or "-", starting with a letter or digit.
volumeName.exists: A volume named {{value}} already exists. Docker would return the existing one without applying these changes.

volumeOpt.unknownLocal: The local driver only uses type, device and o: "{{key}}" will be sent anyway.
volumeOpt.deviceWithoutType: "device" usually needs "type" (e.g. none with o=bind, nfs or tmpfs).

dupNotes.composeLabels: Compose labels were removed: the duplicate won't belong to the project.
dupNotes.portsConflict: The same host ports are in use by the original; change them or stop the original before starting.
dupNotes.mountTypeUnsupported: There are mounts of a type the wizard doesn't support (tmpfs, npipe…).
dupNotes.namedVolumesShared: Named volumes are shared with the original, not copied.
dupNotes.extraNetworks: Only the first network is connected; the others are not carried over.
dupNotes.dns: DNS settings are not carried over.
dupNotes.securityOpt: Security options (--security-opt) are not carried over.
dupNotes.tmpfs: tmpfs mounts are not carried over.
dupNotes.cpuset: Pinned CPUs (--cpuset-cpus) are not carried over.
dupNotes.pidsLimit: The process limit is not carried over.
dupNotes.logConfig: Logging configuration is not carried over.
dupNotes.healthcheck: The custom health check is not carried over.
dupNotes.stopSignal: The custom stop signal is not carried over.
dupNotes.imageMissing: The original image is no longer on this computer: its defaults could not be separated.

pull.title: Pull image
pull.referenceHint: Name with optional tag: nginx:1.27, user/app, registry.example.com:5000/app:v2. Without a tag, latest is used.

authHint.dockerConfig: Like docker pull: uses the credentials saved with docker login (or its credential helper), if there are any for that registry.
authHint.manual: For this pull only: they are not saved anywhere and don't appear in the activity panel.

search.title: Search Docker Hub
search.hint: Docker Engine runs the search on Docker Hub (docker search); Docker needs Internet access.
search.failedHint: If Docker has no access to the Internet or Docker Hub, searching is not possible.
search.name: Name

imageDetail.notFound: Image {{name}} no longer exists in Docker.
imageDetail.localOnly: none (image built or imported on this computer)
imageDetail.layersSummary_one: {{count}} history entry, {{data}} with data, {{size}} in total.
imageDetail.layersSummary_other: {{count}} history entries, {{data}} with data, {{size}} in total.
imageDetail.inspectHint: Full output of docker image inspect {{name}}, exactly as Docker returns it.

imageOps.repositoryHint: For example myapp, user/myapp or registry.example.com:5000/myapp.
imageOps.removeTagBody: This tag is removed. If it is the only one, Docker also removes the image and its unused layers.
imageOps.removeImageBody: The image and the layers no other image uses are removed. This cannot be undone: you would have to pull or build it again.
imageOps.runningRefuses: Docker won't remove an image used by a running container, even when forced: stop and remove it first.
imageOps.stoppedNeedForce: Removing it requires forcing; the containers will still exist, but without their image you won't be able to recreate them.
imageOps.forceMulti: Needed to remove an image with several tags (--force).
imageOps.forceUsed: Needed because stopped containers use it (--force).
imageOps.removed: {{untagged}} tags removed and {{deleted}} layers or images deleted.
imageOps.pruneDangling: Only untagged images no container uses
imageOps.pruneAll: All images no container uses, including tagged ones
imageOps.pruneEstimate_one: Based on the current list, {{count}} image would be removed ({{size}}).
imageOps.pruneEstimate_other: Based on the current list, {{count}} images would be removed ({{size}}).
imageOps.pruneNote: Docker makes the final decision and also removes the related build cache. This cannot be undone.
imageOps.pruneSure: I understand I will have to pull or build those images again
imageOps.pruneWhilePulling_one: {{count}} download is in progress. Wait for it to finish: with the containerd image store, Docker makes ongoing downloads fail when pruning.
imageOps.pruneWhilePulling_other: {{count}} downloads are in progress. Wait for them to finish: with the containerd image store, Docker makes ongoing downloads fail when pruning.

build.title: Build image

g.contextHint: Folder whose contents are sent to Docker (honoring .dockerignore) and the Dockerfile inside it.
g.tagsHint: repository:tag of the resulting image (docker build --tag). Without a name, the image shows as <none>.
g.argsHint: Values for ARG instructions (--build-arg). They stay in the image history: don't use them for secrets.

h.dockerfile: Path relative to the context folder.
h.buildKit: Docker's current builder (the one docker build uses).
h.classic: The previous, deprecated builder; same as DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0 docker build.

build.outsideContext: The Dockerfile must be inside the context folder.
build.secretsHidden_one: {{count}} sensitive value is shown as ******** here and in the activity panel.
build.secretsHidden_other: {{count}} sensitive values are shown as ******** here and in the activity panel.
build.contextPending: Choose a folder with a Dockerfile.
build.special_one: {{count}} special file (socket, device or FIFO) is not sent.
build.special_other: {{count}} special files (sockets, devices or FIFOs) are not sent.
build.unreadable: Cannot read: {{files}}. The build would fail.
build.bigContext: The context is large: consider excluding folders with .dockerignore.

networks.search: Search by name, ID, subnet or container
networks.loadError: Could not get the network list: {{message}}

netDetail.noPools: Docker has not assigned subnets to this network.
netDetail.membersHint: Containers that have this network configured, running or not. Addresses only exist while the container is running.
netDetail.inspectHint: Full Docker response, like "docker network inspect {{name}}".

g.ipv4Hint: Optional: without a subnet, Docker picks a free one.
g.optionsHint: Sent as is to the driver (--opt).

h.name: Letters, digits, "_", "." or "-".

driver.bridge: Private network on this machine; containers reach each other by name.
driver.macvlan: Each container gets its own MAC on the physical network. Set the interface in the "parent" option.
driver.ipvlan: Shares the MAC of the physical interface. Set the interface in the "parent" option.
driver.overlay: Network across several machines: requires Docker Swarm.
driver.other: Driver from a plugin installed in Docker.

h.attachable: For overlay networks: lets standalone containers connect (--attachable).
h.ipRange: Part of the subnet Docker assigns automatically.
h.ipv6: Requires IPv6 support in the kernel and Docker (--ipv6).

netOps.removeBody: The network is removed. This cannot be undone.
netOps.predefined: Docker creates the bridge, host and none networks and does not allow removing them.
netOps.runningBlocks_one: {{count}} running container is connected: Docker will not remove the network until you disconnect or stop it.
netOps.runningBlocks_other: {{count}} running containers are connected: Docker will not remove the network until you disconnect or stop them.
netOps.stoppedBreak_one: {{count}} stopped container has this network configured. Docker removes it anyway and that container will not start until you disconnect it or recreate the network:
netOps.stoppedBreak_other: {{count}} stopped containers have this network configured. Docker removes it anyway and those containers will not start until you disconnect them or recreate the network:
netOps.stoppedSure: I understand those containers will not start
netOps.pruneBody: User-defined networks without running containers are removed. Predefined networks are not touched.
netOps.pruneEstimate_one: According to the current list, {{count}} network will be removed:
netOps.pruneEstimate_other: According to the current list, {{count}} networks will be removed:
netOps.pruneEstimate_zero: According to the current list, there are no networks to remove.
netOps.pruneStoppedWarn_one: {{count}} of those networks is configured in stopped containers: Docker removes it anyway and those containers will not start.
netOps.pruneStoppedWarn_other: {{count}} of those networks are configured in stopped containers: Docker removes them anyway and those containers will not start.
netOps.pruned_zero: There were no networks to remove.
netOps.containerHint: It can be connected running or stopped.

block.already: It is already connected to this network.
block.host: Containers in host mode cannot join other networks, and others cannot join the host network.
block.none: A container without networking (none) cannot join other networks, and others cannot join the none network.

netOps.aliasesHint: Extra names other containers on the network can use to reach it, separated by spaces.
netOps.noAliases: The predefined bridge network does not support aliases.
netOps.ipHint: Inside {{subnets}}. Docker only accepts a fixed IP if the subnet was set when creating the network.
netOps.ipAuto: Docker only accepts a fixed IP if the subnet was set when creating the network.
netOps.disconnectRunning: The container is running: it loses connectivity through this network immediately.
netOps.disconnectStopped: The container no longer has this network configured.
netOps.forceHint: Only if Docker cannot disconnect it normally (--force).
netOps.checking: Checking the current state with Docker…

volumes.sizesNote: Sizes calculated by Docker ("docker system df -v"); this may take a while with large volumes.
volumes.search: Search by name, driver, container or label
volumes.emptyBody: Create a volume to keep data that outlives containers.
volumes.loadError: Could not get the volume list: {{message}}

volDetail.inspectHint: Full Docker response, like "docker volume inspect {{name}}".

volCreate.title: Create volume

g.optionsHint: For the local driver they match those of "mount": type, device and o.

h.name: Optional: without a name Docker creates an anonymous volume. Letters, digits, "_", "." or "-" (at least 2).

preset.plain: Directory managed by Docker on this machine (the usual choice).
preset.tmpfs: In memory: lost when the last container using it stops.
preset.nfs: NFS share: adjust the server address and the path.
preset.bind: Named volume that points to an existing folder on this machine.
preset.other: Driver from a plugin installed in Docker.

volCreate.readyAnonymous: Ready to create an anonymous volume.

volOps.removeBody: The volume and all its data are removed. This cannot be undone.
volOps.inUse_one: {{count}} container mounts it: Docker does not remove a volume in use, not even by a stopped container. Remove the container first.
volOps.inUse_other: {{count}} containers mount it: Docker does not remove a volume in use, not even by stopped containers. Remove the containers first.
volOps.sure: I understand its data will be deleted
volOps.pruneAnonymous: Only anonymous volumes not mounted by any container
volOps.pruneAll: All volumes not mounted by any container (named ones too)
volOps.legacy: This Docker version (API {{api}}) removes all unused volumes, named ones too: it does not distinguish anonymous from named.
volOps.pruneEstimate_one: According to the current state, {{count}} volume will be removed
volOps.pruneEstimate_other: According to the current state, {{count}} volumes will be removed
volOps.pruneEstimate_zero: According to the current state, there are no volumes to remove
volOps.pruneNote: An unused volume may hold important data (for example, from a database whose container you removed).
volOps.pruneSure_one: I understand the data of {{count}} named volume will be deleted
volOps.pruneSure_other: I understand the data of {{count}} named volumes will be deleted
volOps.pruned_zero: There were no volumes to remove.

binds.intro: Folders on this machine mounted inside containers. Docker cannot add mounts to an existing container: to bind a folder, a new container is created with the wizard.
binds.permissions: Permissions and owner on this machine
binds.newContainerHint: Opens the container wizard with this folder already bound

risk.dockerSocket: Docker socket: the container can control Docker and, in practice, the whole machine (except with rootless Docker).
risk.hostRoot: The root of this machine's file system.

binds.riskWritable: It is mounted writable: the container can modify it.
binds.missing: It does not exist on this machine. If the container was created with "-v", Docker creates it again, empty (as root), when starting it.
binds.attentionBanner_one: {{count}} bind needs attention (Docker socket, system directory or missing folder).
binds.attentionBanner_other: {{count}} binds need attention (Docker socket, system directories or missing folders).
binds.emptyBody: Bind a folder so a container can work with files on this machine.
binds.loadError: Could not get the container list: {{message}}

composeList.intro: Projects with containers in Docker (detected by their labels) and the ones you add to the list. Every operation runs the official Docker Compose and is recorded in the activity panel with the exact command.
composeList.search: Search by name, folder or service
composeList.loadError: Could not get the project list: {{message}}
composeList.emptyBody: Open a project you already have (its compose.yaml file) or create a new one. Projects deployed from the terminal show up here automatically.

composeDetail.loadingModel: Reading the file with Docker Compose…
composeDetail.needsValid: Fix the file first: Compose rejects it
composeDetail.registerHint: Keep the project in the list even if its containers are removed
composeDetail.unregisterHint: Only removes it from the list: Docker and the files are not touched
composeDetail.gone: Project “{{name}}” no longer has containers and is not in the list.
composeDetail.missingFiles: These files cannot be found: {{files}}. You can stop, start, view logs or remove the project; deploying it needs the files.
composeDetail.noFiles: Docker does not report the files of this project. You can stop, start, view logs or remove it.
composeDetail.invalidConfig: Docker Compose rejects the project configuration:
composeDetail.noConfig: There is no configuration to show (the files are missing).
composeDetail.configHint: Final configuration as Docker Compose understands it (files merged, variables substituted, all profiles).
composeDetail.secretsWarn: The resolved configuration includes variable values (for example, passwords from the .env file). It is only shown in this window and is not stored in the activity panel.

composeOps.none: No operation has been run on this project yet.
composeOps.dropped_one: {{count}} old line was discarded to limit memory use.
composeOps.dropped_other: {{count}} old lines were discarded to limit memory use.
composeOps.stoppedNote: Docker Compose was interrupted. Whatever it had already done (containers created, images pulled…) is kept.
composeOps.upBody: Creates or updates the project containers, networks and volumes and leaves them running (docker compose up --detach).
composeOps.allServices: With no selection every service is deployed (except those in inactive profiles).
composeOps.someServices: Only the chosen services and the ones they need (depends_on).
composeOps.profilesHint: Services with a profile are only deployed if you enable their profile or pick them above.
composeOps.buildHint: For services with build: (otherwise they are only built if the image does not exist).
composeOps.forceRecreate: Recreate containers even if they have not changed
composeOps.removeOrphansHint: From services that are no longer in the file.
composeOps.downBody_one: {{count}} project container and its networks will be stopped and removed (docker compose down). Volumes and images are kept unless you say otherwise.
composeOps.downBody_other: The {{count}} project containers and their networks will be stopped and removed (docker compose down). Volumes and images are kept unless you say otherwise.
composeOps.downVolumes: Also remove the project's named volumes
composeOps.downVolumesUnknown: The ones declared in the file (or labelled with the project).
composeOps.downVolumesWarn: Data stored in those volumes will be lost permanently.

imagesHint.local: Removes images without a custom tag (the ones Compose builds).
imagesHint.all: Removes every image used by the services, including pulled ones.

composeOps.downSure: I understand the project containers and networks will be removed

composeAdd.title: Open project
composeAdd.body: Choose the project's compose.yaml file. If it uses several files (for example a base file and an override), add them in the order they are merged.
composeAdd.order: They are merged in this order: later files override earlier ones.
composeAdd.name: Project name (optional)
composeAdd.namePh: the one set by the file or folder
composeAdd.nameHint: If left empty, the name Docker Compose decides is used (the file's name: or the folder name).
composeAdd.badName: Only lowercase letters, digits, - and _, starting with a letter or digit.

composeFile.hint: Saving first validates the content with Docker Compose (without saving it). The file is not overwritten if another program changed it in the meantime.
composeFile.readOnly: You do not have permission to modify this file: it is shown read-only.
composeFile.conflict: The file has changed on disk since you opened it. Nothing was saved, so those changes are not lost.
composeFile.saveInvalid: Docker Compose rejects this content. You can keep editing or save it anyway.
composeFile.discard: You have unsaved changes in this file.

composeLogs.paused: Paused: logs are not being received

composeNew.title: New project
composeNew.nameHint: If you type a name, it is added to the file (name:) so the terminal uses the same one. Otherwise Docker Compose uses the folder name.
composeNew.exists: This folder already has a Docker Compose file ({{file}}). It is not overwritten.
composeNew.editorHint: compose.yaml will be created in the folder. It is validated with Docker Compose before it is created.

events.search: Search by name, ID, action or image
events.clearViewHint: Only clears the list on screen; saved events are kept.
events.liveOn: Live: changes in Docker appear instantly and refresh the whole application
events.livePaused: Paused: events are still received and the application keeps refreshing
events.liveOff: Not connected to Docker: no events are received
events.liveEmpty: Nothing has happened in Docker in this session yet. Create, start or stop something (also from the terminal) and it will show up here.
events.journalIntro: Events the application received while it was open and connected, including previous sessions (the latest 20,000 are kept). If “To” is empty, up to now.
events.journalOff: Saving is disabled in Settings › Activity: new events are not saved.
events.journalCount: Showing {{shown}} of {{total}} matching the filters ({{stored}} saved).
events.journalClearBody: The {{count}} saved events will be deleted from disk. Docker and the operation history are not affected.
events.dockerIntro: Asks Docker for the events it keeps (docker events --since … --until …): it includes what happened while the application was closed, but Docker only keeps the latest 256 events in memory and loses them when it restarts. The filter is applied by Docker.
events.truncated: There are more than 5000 events: the most recent are shown.
events.dockerEmpty: Docker keeps no events in that interval with those filters.

history.intro: Operations the application ran on Docker, including previous sessions (the latest 10,000 are kept). What was done, when and with what result are saved; request bodies, equivalent commands and output are not saved because they may contain passwords or other secrets.
history.off: The history is disabled in Settings › Activity: new operations are not saved.
history.search: Search by operation, resource or error
history.count: Showing {{shown}} of {{total}} matching the filters ({{stored}} saved).
history.notKeptBody: The request body, equivalent command and output are only in the activity panel during the session in which it ran.
history.clearBody: The {{count}} saved operations will be deleted from disk. This session's activity panel does not change.
